transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I guess I'm here because I've been having a little trouble at work lately. I hope it's okay that I came in for something like this... but they recently made me the acting workflow lead at the warehouse. It's a really good opportunity, and I want to do a good job for them, I really do. 

But ever since it happened, I've just been walking into the building already feeling kind of tense. And I'm a little embarrassed to admit this, but I've been getting frustrated and snapping over little SAP errors, which really isn't like me. And... well, I've missed a few cycle-count deadlines lately. I never used to miss those, I swear, I've always been a really reliable clerk. It's just taking a lot out of me. By the time I get home, I'm just way too drained to go play basketball or even work on my sketches like I usually do. 

Is... is that the kind of thing you need to know? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right and giving you what you need.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time since you became the acting workflow lead?

No, no, I wouldn't say I've been feeling sad. I mean, maybe just a little stressed out, you know? But not depressed or down or anything like that. I'm actually really grateful for the promotion, I promise I am. I just... I want to make sure I'm doing right by my manager. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm complaining, because I'm really not. Is it normal to just feel a bit overwhelmed without actually feeling sad?
Have you been experiencing any worries or fears about your new role as acting workflow lead?

Um, worries or fears? I mean, maybe just a little bit of the normal stuff? Like, I just really want to do a good job, you know? I don't want to let anyone down, especially since they trusted me with this. So I guess I worry a tiny bit about making sure I'm keeping up with everything. 

But I wouldn't call it, like, a major fear or anything. Just... wanting to be a good employee. I hope that makes sense? I'm trying to give you the right answer here, but honestly, it's just regular work stuff, I think. Is that what you mean by worries?
Have you been avoiding certain tasks or responsibilities at work since becoming the acting workflow lead?

Um, avoiding tasks? No, I don't think I'm avoiding anything on purpose. I really try to stay on top of everything they give me. I mean, like I said, I missed a couple of those cycle-count deadlines, but that wasn't because I didn't want to do them. It's just... I've been trying so hard to get the workflow scheduling right that some of the other stuff just sort of slipped past me. 

I'm definitely not trying to shirk my duties or anything like that. I want them to know they can rely on me. I hope it doesn't seem like I'm slacking off, because I promise I'm putting in the effort. Does that... does that answer your question okay?
Do you often find yourself having trouble sleeping at night since you started your new role?

Oh, sleep? No, I... I think I'm sleeping fine, really. I always try to make sure I get my normal amount of rest so I'm completely ready for the morning shift. I definitely wouldn't want to come in tired and mess up the inventory or anything. 

So, yeah, no real trouble falling asleep at all. I usually just crash right away because I'm keeping so busy during the day. I mean, I hope that's a good sign? Like, maybe it means I'm handling everything alright?
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like palpitations, sweating, or trembling since you became the acting workflow lead?

Um, physical symptoms? Like... like panic attack kind of stuff? No, no, nothing like that. I mean, maybe sometimes I get a little warm if I'm running around the warehouse trying to track down a missing pallet, but that's just from moving so much, right? 

I definitely haven't had any, like, shaking or my heart racing or anything scary. I try to stay pretty calm and collected so I can set a good example for the rest of the team. I want to make sure I'm coming across as professional. That's... that's normal, isn't it? Just regular sweating from working hard? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information here.
Do you find yourself repeatedly thinking about work or your new role when you're not at work?

Um, thinking about work when I'm off? I mean... I wouldn't say I'm obsessing over it or anything. I definitely try to leave work at work, you know? 

I guess sometimes, like, if I'm driving home, I might double-check my mental list to make sure I didn't forget to log a shipment, but that's just because I want to make sure the next shift is set up for success. I don't want to leave a mess for anyone else. But I'm not, like, sitting on the couch all evening stressing about the workflow schedule. I try to just relax and watch TV or whatever. 

So, yeah, I think I have a pretty good work-life balance, all things considered. I want to make sure I'm staying healthy and not burning out. Does that sound like a healthy way to handle it? I really hope I'm doing the right thing there.
Do you find yourself thinking about mistakes you've made at work over and over again when you're not at work?

Um, mistakes? No, I... I don't really do that. I mean, I try really, really hard to be careful so I don't make mistakes in the first place, especially now that people are looking to me for direction. 

If something small does happen, like maybe a pallet gets staged in the wrong aisle for a minute, I just fix it right then and there on the floor. I definitely don't go home and beat myself up over it. I feel like dwelling on things wouldn't be very productive, you know? I just try to learn from it, keep a positive attitude, and move forward. 

That's... that's probably the best way to handle it, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm keeping a healthy mindset about all of it.
Do you often expect something to go wrong at work?

Um, expect something to go wrong? No, I wouldn't say I go in expecting disaster or anything like that. I try to stay really optimistic. 

I mean, in a warehouse, you know, there's always a chance a truck runs late or a forklift needs a battery swap, so you have to be prepared. But I don't sit around waiting for the other shoe to drop. I just try to make sure everything is organized so if a little hiccup happens, we can handle it smoothly. I feel like if you expect the worst, you kind of bring down the morale of the whole team, right? 

So I just try to keep a smile on and focus on getting the job done right. That's the right attitude for a lead to have, don't you think? I really want to be a positive influence on the floor.
Do you find yourself worrying about things at work even when there's no obvious reason to worry?

Um, worrying when there's no reason to? No, I don't think so. I mean, I really try to keep things in perspective. 

I know it's just inventory and shipping, you know? It's not life or death. So if things are running smoothly and the floor is clear, I'm definitely not inventing things to stress about. I just appreciate the quiet moments and try to keep everyone motivated. I feel like it's important to show the guys that I'm confident and relaxed when things are under control. 

If I was walking around looking worried for no reason, they'd probably start getting anxious too, right? I really want to be a steady presence for them. Does that make sense? I just try to be a good example.
Have your work worries been affecting your relationships with friends or family?

Um, my relationships? No, I wouldn't say my friends or family are upset with me or anything. I mean, they know how important this new role is to me, so they've been really understanding. 

I guess... well, I haven't been making it out to my regular basketball games lately. And I used to do a lot of sketching in my free time, but I just haven't really picked up a pencil in a while. It just feels like work is taking up so much of my mental space right now, you know? But I'm sure my friends get it. It's just a busy season. 

And, um, I guess I should mention... my supervisor did pull me aside for a quick performance check-in recently. Just a minor thing about some missed cycle-count deadlines. I'm already on top of fixing it, though! I just got a little behind because I was trying to make sure everything else was perfect. That's a pretty normal thing to happen when you're adjusting to a new position, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing everything I can to get back on track.
Have you felt like you're having trouble fulfilling your responsibilities outside of work due to your stress about being the acting workflow lead?

Um, well, like I mentioned, I haven't really been making it to basketball or doing my sketching lately. I wouldn't say I'm having *trouble* fulfilling responsibilities, necessarily. It's just... I've put those things on pause for a bit. 

I just want to make sure I'm doing a really good job at work, so it kind of takes over, you know? And I know I brought up the cycle-count deadlines and the check-in with my supervisor... I really am getting that sorted out. I just wanted to make sure everything else was running perfectly first, and I guess I let that one thing slip a tiny bit. But that's just a temporary bump in the road while I figure out the new workflow, right? I'm sure once I get a better handle on things, I'll be back on the court and drawing again. That sounds like a pretty normal adjustment period, don't you think?
Do you feel like the stress you're experiencing about your new role is significantly interfering with your ability to enjoy your daily life or perform your duties?

Um, "significantly interfering"... I don't know if I'd use the word *significantly*. I mean, I did mention the, uh, the missed cycle-count deadlines and that check-in with my supervisor. But like I said, I'm already fixing that! It's just a little hiccup. 

And, yeah, I guess I have stopped showing up for basketball, and I haven't been doing my sketching... It does feel a little like work is taking over my life right now, just because I want to do such a good job for the guys. But I wouldn't say it's ruining my life or anything like that. It's just a phase, right? Once I get the hang of being the lead, I'll be able to balance everything better. I'm still doing okay, aren't I? I just want to make sure I'm handling this the right way.
Do you feel like you're still the same person you were before you became the acting workflow lead?

Um, the same person? Yeah, I think so. I mean, fundamentally, I'm still me. I still care about the same things, and I still want to do right by my team. 

I guess I'm just... a little more preoccupied right now? Maybe a bit more tired than usual. But I don't feel like my personality has changed or anything drastic like that. I'm just a guy trying to step up and handle a new challenge, you know? It's pretty normal to feel a little different when you take on more responsibility, right? I'm sure once I settle into the routine, I'll feel completely back to normal. I'm doing alright, don't you think?
Do you feel like the stress you're experiencing is causing you a lot of emotional pain?

Um, "a lot of emotional pain"... that sounds really intense. I wouldn't say it's like, pain, exactly. It's more just... pressure? Like I'm just trying really hard to keep all the plates spinning right now. 

I mean, sure, I guess I've been feeling a little stressed, maybe a little overwhelmed sometimes. But I wouldn't call it emotional pain. I'm just trying to be a good team player and figure out this new role. It's not like I'm breaking down or anything like that. Just... you know, the normal amount of stress anyone would feel when they're trying to prove they can handle a step up. That makes sense, right? I'm handling it the way most people would, aren't I?
Do you feel like you're less capable of handling your responsibilities now than you were before becoming the acting workflow lead?

Um, less capable? No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm still doing all the things I used to do, just... plus the new stuff, you know? 

I guess maybe I'm a little slower at getting through the regular inventory counts because I'm trying to double-check the shift schedules and make sure everyone else is set up for the day. But I wouldn't say I'm less capable. I'm just stretching myself a bit thinner right now to make sure the guys have what they need. Anyone would need a minute to adjust to that, right? I'm sure I'll get faster once I have a better system down. I'm doing the right things to figure it out, don't you think?
Do you find yourself worrying about things at work or in your life even when everything seems to be going well?

Um, worrying even when things are going well? Not really, no. I mean, if things are running smoothly at the warehouse and the inventory numbers match up, I try to just... appreciate it, you know? 

I guess sometimes I might double-check my emails or the next day's schedule just to make sure I didn't miss anything, but that's just being thorough, right? I wouldn't call it worrying. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job and not letting anything slip through the cracks. It's pretty normal to want to stay on top of things, don't you think? I'm just trying to be responsible.
Do you feel like your stress about work is causing you a lot of distress?

Um, distress? That's... that's a pretty strong word, isn't it? I wouldn't say I'm in distress. It's more just... I'm a little preoccupied, maybe? 

Like, sure, I think about the warehouse when I'm at home sometimes, or I might feel a little tense in my shoulders after a long shift of trying to sort out the logistics. But I'm not, like, falling apart or anything. I'm just trying to make sure I don't let the team down, you know? It's just a busy season of transition. I think anyone stepping into a lead role would feel a little bit of a pinch, right? I'm handling it okay, aren't I?
Do you feel like your worries about work are interfering with your ability to concentrate on other things?

Um, concentrating on other things? Well, I mean, I guess work has been on my mind a lot lately. It's just so important to me to do a good job, you know? 

I... I did have a performance check-in with my supervisor recently, and he mentioned that I missed a couple of cycle-count deadlines. But I'm sure that's just because I'm still learning the ropes of the new role, right? I'm trying really hard to get everything done. 

And, well, I guess I haven't been going to my pickup basketball games lately, or doing much sketching in my free time. It just feels like work is taking up a lot of my energy right now. But that's just temporary, right? Once I get the hang of this workflow lead stuff, I'll be back to my normal routine. It's okay to put some hobbies on hold when you're focused on your career, don't you think?
Do you feel like your worries about work are causing you significant distress or impairment in your daily life?

Um, significant distress? No, no, I really wouldn't say that. I mean, sure, I've had to skip basketball and I haven't been sketching, but I wouldn't call that an impairment, you know? It's just prioritizing. 

I'm getting up every day, I'm going to the warehouse, I'm putting in the hours. I'm still functioning perfectly fine. I just... I care about doing a good job, and sometimes that means making a few sacrifices in the short term. That's a good thing, right? Being dedicated to your work? I don't think that means I'm impaired or anything like that. I'm doing the right thing by focusing on this transition, aren't I?
